correctness.rationale: Gaussian projection to the sum-zero hyperplane gives exact W=2 sqrt(2) M/(sqrt(n-1) R), M=max_{ij in E}|g_i-g_j|/sqrt(2), R^2=chi²_{n-1}/(n-1). Disjoint edge increments are independent; adjacent increments have |correlation|=1/2, yielding joint tail <=4 exp(-2u²/3). Bounded-degree dependency components contribute o(1) to fixed factorial moments at u=b+x/b, while singleton components converge to Poisson mean exp(-x), giving the Gumbel law; chi correction is negligible since b²=O(log n). To prove uniform angular probability, integrate the independent far-edge maximum distribution against uniform variable m*p(Y_e), dominate by a linearly large matching, and exclude nearby wins with the same m^-4/3 joint tail; each orientation gets half the winning-edge probability. For star, leaf upper/lower extrema combine with one common center Gaussian to give |Z|. Independent checks: 150 exact support identities, 11,500 path samples at n=850 with empirical CDF 0.3792 vs exp(-1)=0.3679, star sample mean 0.998 vs asymptotic 0.798 (visible finite-n centering bias). No finite result proves the asymptotic law.
